extracted.intended_audience: Isabelle users and Archive of Formal Proofs (AFP) contributors/users
extracted.subtask_description: Instructions for making the Archive of Formal Proofs available to Isabelle, importing AFP articles into your theories, preferred citation/bibtex format for AFP entries, and relevant mailing lists. Focused on practical steps and recommended formats.

rubrics_metrics.name: Making the whole AFP available to Isabelle
rubrics_metrics.description: From Isabelle2021-1 on, the recommended method for making the whole AFP available to Isabelle is the isabelle components -u command.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: on Linux/Mac, assuming afp is unzipped to /home/myself/afp, run: isabelle components -u /home/myself/afp/thys. On Windows (use Cygwin terminal), if the AFP is in C:\afp, run: isabelle components -u /cygdrive/c/afp/thys. (Assumes you have downloaded and unzipped the afp.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Referring to AFP entries in imports
rubrics_metrics.description: You can now refer to article ABC from the AFP in another theory via: imports "ABC.Some_ABC_Theory".
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This allows you to distribute your material separately from any AFP theories. Note that users of your distribution also need to install the AFP in the manner described above.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preferred citation format for AFP entries
rubrics_metrics.description: Preferred way for citing entries in the AFP is given as a bibliographic citation example: 'M. Jaskelioff and S. Merz, Proving the Correctness of Disk Paxos. Archive of Formal Proofs, June 2005, https://isa-afp.org/entries/DiskPaxos.html, Formal proof development.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the example citation format (author, title, Archive of Formal Proofs, month, year, URL, brief descriptor) when referencing AFP entries in publications or documentation.

rubrics_metrics.name: BibTeX entry structure for AFP articles
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide a bibtex @article entry for AFP items including author, title, journal, month, year, note (with URL and descriptor), and ISSN.
rubrics_metrics.guidance:
Example provided in page: @article{DiskPaxos-AFP,
  author =   {Mauro Jaskelioff and Stephan Merz},
  title =    {Proving the Correctness of Disk Paxos},
  journal =  {Archive of Formal Proofs},
  month =    {June},
  year =     {2005},
  note =     {\url{https://isa-afp.org/entries/DiskPaxos.html}, Formal proof development},
  ISSN =     {2150-914x}
}
Include the URL and a brief descriptor in the note field and include the AFP ISSN where appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mailing lists and their purposes
rubrics_metrics.description: isabelle-users@cl.cam.ac.uk provides a forum for Isabelle users to discuss problems, exchange information, and make announcements. isabelle-dev@in.tum.de covers the Isabelle development process, including intermediate repository versions, and administrative issues concerning the website or testing infrastructure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Users of official Isabelle releases should subscribe or consult the isabelle-users archive. Early adopters of development snapshots or repository versions (and those interested in website/testing/admin issues) should subscribe to isabelle-dev or consult its archive (also available at mail-archive.com).
